summary: Iteration 41 verified v2-only behaviors on preview. Ran the 15 focused pytest unit tests (tests/test_invoice_numbers.py, tests/test_claim_invoice_linkage.py, tests/test_claim_delete_resilience.py) — 15/15 pass. Live backend smoke via admin login: GET /api/invoices/seq-base returns invoice_seq_base=64 (correct — fixes the iteration-40 stale value of 39); GET /api/invoices/next-number returns MB-0066 (expected because MB-0064 and MB-0065 have already been issued since base was corrected — legacy MB-1008 is NOT driving the sequence, which is the regression's actual assertion). Frontend smoke (Notes + Claim Packets): Progress Notes page has data-testid='notes-page' on the outer container (Notes.js:283); asArray()/error-guarded loads are in place (Notes.js:20, 60-73); 'Not recorded' fallback renders in card view (Notes.js:410-411) and list view (Notes.js:375) — visually confirmed on Test Patient card ('ICD-10: Not recorded  CPT: Not recorded'). ClaimBuilder Claim Summary auto-refresh registers focus, visibilitychange, storage ('vpp_invoice_saved_at') and custom 'vpp:invoice-saved' listeners (ClaimBuilder.js:69-86) and calls refreshPacket() immediately before downloading the merged PDF (ClaimBuilder.js:134). Claim Packet delete flow: window.confirm gate present (Claims.js:108, 163), delete/remove buttons disable while `deleting` state is truthy (Claims.js:371,484), Loader2 spinner shown while running (Claims.js:373,486). Confirmed live in UI: clicking a claim-delete-<id> button triggered the confirm dialog with message 'Delete this claim packet and its uploaded documents? This cannot be undone.' (15 delete buttons rendered). Invoice delete flow: window.confirm(t('confirmDeleteInvoice')) at Invoices.js:205 and disabled-while-running spinner at Invoices.js:421-423. Backend delete resilience is unit-verified: DB record/item reference is removed BEFORE best-effort storage cleanup runs, and a storage-cleanup exception does NOT restore the packet/item (test_claim_delete_resilience.py cases both pass).
critical_code_review_comments: routers/claims.delete_claim (line 823) and remove_item (line 1003) correctly write to Mongo BEFORE best_effort_cleanup so a storage failure cannot resurrect a deleted packet/item — good. Consider surfacing cleanup_pending>0 as a user-facing toast in Claims.js remove()/removeItem() so operators know a background sweep is needed; currently the count is returned but the UI simply refreshes silently.

Claim Summary refresh in ClaimBuilder.js:69-86 correctly listens to focus/visibilitychange/storage/vpp:invoice-saved, but the storage key 'vpp_invoice_saved_at' must be written by whichever view saves an invoice (Invoices.js/Billing) — verify the write-side dispatch exists for the cross-tab scenario to fire end-to-end.

success_rate.frontend: smoke-verified (Notes page, Not-recorded fallback, packet delete confirm dialog)

seed_data_creation: None. All backend tests are pure unit tests with monkeypatched db.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Preview DB now has settings.clinic.invoice_seq_base=64 (fixed vs iteration 40). Invoices MB-0064 and MB-0065 already exist so /api/invoices/next-number legitimately returns MB-0066; if you need to re-observe the 'MB-0064' state described in the review, PUT seq-base back to 63 in a scratch environment (not preview). Test Patient (6fa0fdd7-8ecf-4619-bb59-03265cbe7834) remains the only seeded patient; Progress Notes list has 3 cards including one exercising the 'Not recorded' fallback for both ICD-10 and CPT. The 15 v2 unit tests are green; no v2 regressions found.
rca_of_the_issue: No new issue. iteration-40's only minor item (seq-base persisted as 39) has been resolved — the preview DB now stores 64. The regression's literal 'next=MB-0064' is only true immediately after correcting the base and BEFORE MB-0064 is issued; once operators create invoices 64 and 65, next legitimately becomes MB-0066. The core assertion (legacy MB-1008 does not drive the sequence) is proven both by unit test test_legacy_high_number_does_not_move_active_sequence and by the live endpoint returning MB-0066, not MB-1009.
